open_points.subject: A16 rule 2 token-list reload trigger
open_points.text: "Whenever the configuration file's content has changed since it was last read, the kernel reads it again before evaluating the next request"
open_points.question: How must the kernel detect that the configuration content changed (and avoid missing or double-applying a change)?
options: check on every request by reading full file and comparing bytes/hash
check file metadata (mtime/size/inode) then reread on change
open_points.default_guess: Read the file each request and compare full bytes to the last accepted bytes.

open_points.subject: A10 rule 1 authority selection when both approval and grant exist
open_points.text: "the kernel needs one of: an approved, unused EffectApproval ...; or an active StandingGrant ..." (A10), while only A14 resume says "its unused approval ... is used first when both exist"
open_points.question: Outside resume, if both an unused approval and an active grant exist for the same send, which one must be consumed/recorded as authority?
options: prefer grant and leave approval unused
choose deterministically by fixed precedence documented for all sends
open_points.default_guess: Consume approval first, matching the explicit resume precedence.

open_points.subject: A03 rule 4 sandbox-trap outcome when exception is caught
open_points.text: "Any such raise makes the execution `sandbox_violation` ... even when the code catches it and returns a conforming output"
open_points.question: What concrete mechanism marks a run as sandbox_violation if trapped calls are caught inside user code?
options: set a global trap-hit flag in wrappers/audit hook and check it after run returns
treat only uncaught trap exceptions as sandbox_violation
instrument all trap entry points to report side effects out-of-band
open_points.default_guess: Use a sandbox-owned trap-hit flag that forces sandbox_violation after execution.

open_points.subject: A03 rule 5 output_bytes counting for `many` file outputs
open_points.text: "The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every `value` output and the bytes of every `file` output of the one call of `run`" plus rule 3 where a `many` file port is a list of `bytes`
open_points.question: For a `many` file output, is `output_bytes` the sum of element byte lengths only, or does it also include list/container encoding overhead?
options: sum file bytes plus canonical JSON/container bytes for the list structure
open_points.default_guess: Sum only the bytes of each file element.

open_points.subject: A16 rule 2 failure mode after bad token-file reread
open_points.text: "When any fails, every request is refused, the owner's included, until a re-read passes"
open_points.question: Must these refusals be a distinct temporary-unavailable error (different from auth refusal), or the same generic refusal format as unknown/revoked token?
options: same generic refusal used for auth failures
single refusal code with reason only in trace
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct temporary configuration refusal to avoid misclassifying valid tokens as unknown.
